newsitem.title: GERMANY: HP says to grow faster than German market.
newsitem.headline: HP says to grow faster than German market.

text.p: Computer and printer maker Hewlett-Packard Co. said Tuesday that its net earnings at its German subsidiary fell last year but would grow faster than the market in 1997.

The company said profits after taxes slipped to 127 million marks ($74.4 million) in the year ending Oct. 31 from 141 million ($82.6 million) the year before, when earnings benefited from tax bonuses not available in 1996.

"In Europe and in Germany market developments have been rather moderate since the middle of last year," the company said in a statement. "Management is confident that this year Hewlett-Packard will again grow more strongly than the market."

Because of an accounting change, sales in Germany fell to 8.3 billion marks (4.86 billion) from 8.7 billion ($5.1 billion) the year before. The decline resulted from a transfer of accounting for internal sales to HP's Europe headquarters in the Netherlands.
